To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

parallelism in a database operation can be realized by simply using more threads, that the degree of parallelism in a given database operation is independent of the number of cores available on a processor, that the degree to which an operation can benefit from parallelization depends on the operation's characteristics and that the number of cores that a processor can support has a direct effect on the degree of parallelization that a database operation can realize.

1) parallelism in database systems can be achieved easily on massively multithread- ed processors; 2) parallelism can be exploited with little effort; 3) parallelism can scale with the number of processor cores; and 4) database performance can be increased by orders of magnitude.

(1) the degree of parallelism in database queries can be made to increase linearly with the degree of parallel processing available on the MTA2; (2) the degree of thread-level parallelism in database systems is significantly greater than that found in traditional scientific codes; and (3) the degree of data-level parallelism in scientific codes is greater than the degree of data-parallelism in database systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the question, “What can be gained by using massively multithread- ed processors to perform database operations?”
the question of how well database operations can be parallelized in the presence of increased on-chip multicores and multithreads.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MTA- 2 architecture has been a good testbed for the study of database operations on a massively multithreading platform, and that this research is a good example of the kind of work that is needed to make the best possible use of the new generation of multicore and multihreaded architectures.
parallelism in databases is easy and that, with the right architecture, it can scale linearly with available cores.
the Cray M.T.A-2 architecture is not suitable for the execution of database applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parallelism in databases is not a problem; it is the lack of support for parallelism in databases that is the problem.
the MTA- 2 provides an excellent platform on which to explore parallelism in database systems.
parallelism in the database domain is easy to achieve, but it requires careful design and implementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, as the number of processor cores per chip increases, database systems will have to be designed with a much greater degree of parallelism in mind.
the degree of parallelism in database applications is limited by the amount of work that can be done per core, not by the amount of data.
parallelism in the database can be easily exploited with the use of a massively multithreading architecture, and that the use of such architectures can lead to substantial performance improvements.
